rules._comment_ask: Old policy had these as ask; keep human-in-the-loop. (git commit was flipped to ask in your last manual config edit - preserved.)
rules._comment_allow: Write-side / project-tooling commands you used to allow by whitelist. These are the 'known-good long tail' that would otherwise hit the reviewer model every time (cost + latency). gotgenes path/external layers still bound them: an allowed 'cp' can still not touch ~/.ssh or escape the working tree. Narrowed 2026-09: docker only for read-only inspection subcommands (docker run/exec can mount $HOME and escape every path rule - those now go to the reviewer); curl removed (read-vs-exfil is exactly the reviewer's judgment call, and friction grows narrow rules via deny & remember as designed); pi narrowed to 'pi list' (config/install/remove/update mutate the gate stack itself; nested 'pi -p' escapes the outer session's gating).

_comment_purpose: LAYER 2/3 of the permission stack: semantic BASH judgment (replaces the deleted 150-line gotgenes whitelist). See home/.pi/agent/extensions/README.md in the dotfiles repo for the full architecture. NOTE: this file is strict JSON (menshen uses JSON.parse) - comments live in _comment keys.
_comment_gatedTools: We deliberately gate ONLY 'bash' here. write/edit/mcp/path decisions stay with gotgenes (deterministic, symlink-aware, cross-cutting - see pi-permission-system/config.json). Menshen's value is its tree-sitter AST + read-only registry + reviewer model, which is exactly the bash-command question gotgenes cannot answer.
_comment_classifierModel: Empty = reviewer model for the long tail is the current session model. Pinned to a cheap fast-tier opencode-go model so reviews stay low-latency (reviewer thinking is hard-pinned to 'low' by menshen; TTFT is dominated by the model's 'low' budget) and keep the main model's context warm. Chosen from ~/.pi/agent/models-store.json: glm-5.3-flash has explicit low-thinking support + zero cache-write cost (menshen discards/respawns the reviewer trunk on failures, so cache-write pricing matters). Runner-up: deepseek-v4-flash (cheaper cache reads, pricier output). Note: an unresolvable string silently falls back to the session model, so keep the exact 'opencode-go/<id>' format with no ':thinking' suffix.
_comment_sensitivePaths: Menshen-local notion of sensitive: a read-only command touching these goes to REVIEW instead of auto-allow, and in-project writes to them lose the write fast-path. These are NOT hard denies - the hard denies are gotgenes `path` rules (single source of truth). Keep both lists roughly in sync; *.envrc-priv mirrors the gotgenes deny.
_comment_rules: Deterministic rules mirroring the OLD gotgenes bash policy for everything the read-only registry does NOT already cover (plain readers like cat/ls/grep/git log are auto-allowed by the registry - do not re-add them here). Syntax: Tool(prefix:*). deny wins over ask wins over allow; rules are checked BEFORE fast-paths, so deny/ask entries also override the registry. Prefix rules also match the bare command (rules.ts: candidate === prefix), so 'Bash(git push:*)' denies a bare 'git push'. 2026-09: docker/curl/pi broad allows tightened - see _comment_allow.
_comment_removed_from_old_whitelist: Deliberate behavior changes vs the deleted whitelist: (1) 'rm *.go' is NOT allowed anymore - too broad; novel rm forms go to the reviewer model instead. (2) 'cd *' left to the registry. (3) Anything unlisted and non-read-only (npm install, ssh, brew, curl, docker run, ...) now reaches the Guardian reviewer instead of being silently denied - approve a few times with 'deny & remember'/session approvals and menshen grows narrow rules for you.
